notes: target_function is the TickIteratorDown overload of reset (the file has two reset overloads, one per iterator; blank.patch shows exactly which body is blanked). PoV is a revert oracle: the swap underflows and reverts on the vulnerable (start-exclusive) downward walk, so vm.expectRevert catches it and the test PASSES; a correct (start-inclusive) walk lets the swap succeed, the expected revert never happens, and the test FAILS. So PoV passing on agent output = agent reproduced the vulnerability. pov_cmd is scoped with both --match-path and --match-test because PoV63008_AngstromL2 inherits AngstromL2Test; the extra filters run only the one PoV method and do not re-run the parent suite. PoV test is NOT present during the agent run; it is added only at judging. functional_cmd is empty on purpose: the only existing test that exercises the target (test/libraries/TickIterator.t.sol) bakes in the start-exclusive downward behaviour shipped in this audited snapshot (e.g. test_iterateDown_simple starts at 100 and asserts the first tick is 50, not 100), so a correct start-inclusive implementation FAILS its downward assertions and it cannot act as a must-pass-for-a-valid-implementation gate; the fix commit c01b6c7 rewrote that test file (+249/-24) into a liquidity-invariant fuzzing form, and no existing test is a stable pass-for-correct gate for this function. deps are the vendored git-submodule checkouts under lib/ (nested: lib/v4-periphery contains lib/v4-core and lib/permit2); the offline forge build reads them directly, so deps_source points at that lib dir. solc 0.8.26 comes from the shared solvibe-svm Docker volume.
